Checkpoint 40 — CSRF login-lockout fix live (detailed)

The bug

Re-login from a browser holding a stale ldndrc_session cookie → 403 "csrf token missing or invalid", login handler never reached. guardCSRF required a CSRF header on every cookie-carrying POST, but login is the endpoint that issues tokens — it can never require one. Chicken-and-egg lockout.

The fix (on main, uncommitted until this checkpoint)

  • internal/httpapi/csrf.go: early-return the guard for POST /api/auth/login (before the method switch), with comment explaining why. Header comment updated (was: "pre-auth endpoints carry no cookie" — wrong; login carries stale cookies).
  • internal/httpapi/csrf_test.go: regression case in TestCSRFGuard — login POST + stale cookie + no header → 200 (the helper loginTokens was always cookieless, which is why the suite never caught the bug).
  • manifests/control-panel-deployment.yaml: stale comment refresh — Selkies 2.0.0 is live (CP-34/35), not "deferred / 502-by-design".

Proofs before deploy

  • gofmt/go vet clean; full go test -count=1 ./... green (all 7 packages; join 10.3s).
  • Docker image ldndrc/control-panel:dev rebuilt + smoke-tested in a throwaway container: stale-cookie login → 200; cookie-POST without header → 403.

Deploy (observed)

  • First import attempt failed: tarball had been saved to /tmp (tmpfs, wiped) — re-saved to ~/ldndrc-panel-csrffix.tar (14M). Lesson repeated: import tarballs live in $HOME, never /tmp.
  • Scratch-pod import check: a probe pod with the image returned StartError: exec "sh" not found — that error itself proves the image is present in containerd (missing image would be ImagePullBackOff). The panel image is distroless: no shell.
  • Rollout: delete-old-first (kubectl delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=ldndrc-control-panel), new pod vm7c9 Running/ready in ~13s, 0 restarts. (Plain rollout restart stays forbidden — hostNetwork :8082 deadlock, CP-20 §6.)

Live proof matrix (through :8082, Host=control.ros-platform.local)

# Scenario Observed
1 Stale-cookie login POST 200, token+csrf issued
2 Garbage cookie POST /api/sessions, no header 403
3 No cookie, Bearer + CSRF header 202 (session created)
4 Valid cookie + matching header 409 — guard passed; handler's one-session-per-user conflict
5 Valid cookie + wrong header 403 — pairing enforced

Notes on test #3/#4 mechanics (cost me a round-trip each):

  • Login sets the cookie itself (router.go:71 SetSessionCookie), but with COOKIE_DOMAIN=.ros-platform.local curl on 127.0.0.1 won't store it → looked like "no cookie". Use --resolve control.ros-platform.local:8082:127.0.0.1 to test the real path.
  • The wrong-header "negative" without a cookie isn't a guard test at all: no cookie → guard skipped → handler (409 conflict).
  • CSRF pairing model: VerifyCSRF(cookie.Value, header) — the header token is verified against the cookie's JWT.

Environment incident discovered mid-proof

The laptop's WiFi IP drifted 192.168.1.37 → 192.168.1.65 (DHCP). Consequences observed:

  • /etc/hosts entries (line 5) still point at .37 → every *.ros-platform.local URL dead from the browser, even though the panel is healthy (127.0.0.1:8082 → 200). User needs the sudo hosts fix again.
  • manifests/control-panel-deployment.yaml line 81 hardcodes https://192.168.1.37:6443 (join/kubeconfig path). Debt: make the IP configurable or drift-proof (DHCP reservation is the cheap fix).

Nothing live depends on the stale IP for this proof (used 127.0.0.1), but browser-facing UI is unreachable until /etc/hosts is corrected.

Dirty-tree discipline

Committed in this chunk: csrf.go, csrf_test.go, control-panel-deployment.yaml (comment), this report. The 5 untracked junk files left alone. No push.
